source.note: No real product. A generic warm-Japandi visual proxy made for the demo catalogue; it copies no retailer's design and carries no brand.
source.generation: Higgsfield multi_image_to_3d from a four-view AI turnaround sheet generated with the Codex image_gen tool (codex-image.sh); should_texture=true, enable_pbr=true, should_remesh=true, topology=triangle, target_polycount=28000, symmetry_mode=auto, rigging and animation off.
source.postProcessing: @gltf-transform/cli resize --width 1024 --height 1024, then scripts/fit_glb.py per-axis fit (centres the footprint, puts the base at y=0).
source.priceProvenance: invented: a plausible demo figure, not a real or quoted price

knownLimitations: No real product. Generic Japandi visual proxy generated from an AI turnaround sheet; the catalogue price is invented, not sourced.

Best fit of the three: exactly 70.0 x 70.0 x 22.0 cm at 5.99 percent anisotropy, fit_glb.py exited 0. The raw mesh was a circular 189.9 x 189.9 cm plan 56.3 cm tall, a 3.37:1 width-to-height ratio against the listing's 3.18:1, so almost no correction was needed.

A round object gives four nearly identical turnaround views, so the multi-view reconstruction had less independent information than an asymmetric object would; the underside is not visible in any source view and is likely a flat cap, hidden once the cushion sits on the floor (minY 0.0).

Not inspected in a render; no render was available to this agent. The source turnaround sheet showed four views of one low wide drum-shaped floor cushion in washed greige-oatmeal linen, with a piped seam around the top and bottom rim, a single central button tuft, and a straight gusseted side band.
PBR textures resized to 1024 px, so the washed-linen slub texture is softer than the source sheet.
